blocks.0: Hey Hebrew Letter (ה): Sound, Vowels & Practice
blocks.6: Tsere consists of two horizontal dots (צֵ) placed beneath a letter. It produces an [e] sound, similar to the [e] in 'they.'

3.tip: Tsere represents the [e] sound. When combined with Hey (הֵ), it produces [he], like in 'hey.'

12.tip: Kamatz Gadol represents the [a] sound. When the letter Hey (הָ) is marked with Kamatz Gadol, it produces [ha].

theory.heading: Meet Hey
theory.intro: The fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Hey makes a soft [h] sound, and is often silent at the end of a word.
objectives: Hear its soft [h] sound, and notice when it's silent.
Meet two new vowel marks, Tsere and Segol, both pronounced [e].

examples.heading: Tsere, Segol and new words
examples.intro: Meet two new vowel marks that both make an [e] sound, then see Hey in real Hebrew words.
